title: Pebble Retail — partner scout and outbound playbook (scratch)
body:
Quick notes / raw brain dump for Pebble Retail (mid-market omnichannel merchant).

Context: met briefly at NRF 2025 booth demo (Sahil from Redwood intro). Pebble sells POS + headless commerce for boutique retailers — strong COGS focus, customer success org of ~8, recently raised series B (public filing Oct 2024). Looking for ways to turn checkout + receipts -> more revenue without adding headcount.

Why Redwood might land:
- Need for cheap, reliable inference at scale for receipts summarization + personalized offers (on-device/edge not required).
- They already use hosted third-party APIs for embeddings, but flagged cost+latency as blockers.
- Pilot win criterion: meaningfully higher click-through on post-purchase offers and a 10–20% increase in conversion for cross-sell within 14 days.

Account research (quick):
- HQ: Austin, TX. CTO: Morgan Hale (LinkedIn: morgan-hale). Head of Product: Lina Cho. Head of Ops: Derek Ames.
- Tech stack: React storefront, Node/Koa backend, Postgres, Redis. Kubernetes on AWS (EKS).
- Current vendor hints: using third-party vector DB (managed), SSO via Okta, payment via Stripe Connect, analytics via Segment.
- Privacy posture: moderate — will accept PII in-hosted vendor with contract; enterprise-ready security but price sensitive.

Primary use-cases to pitch (order matters):
1) Post-purchase micro-personalization: generate 1–2 sentence tailored recommendations in transactional email or receipt view (low latency, high throughput).
2) In-store associate assistant: quick SKU lookup + prompt-based substitution suggestions (latency SLOs matter here).
3) Search/rerank for product discovery inside merchant portal (embeddings + rerank).
4) Automated policy/return reason summarization (ops efficiency).

Success metrics to propose:
- Pilot length: 6 weeks active + 2-week warmup.
- KPI A: CTR on in-receipt offers (baseline estimate 2–3% -> target 4–6%).
- KPI B: Reduced associate time per lookup (target -18%).
- Technical KPI: 95th percentile inference latency < 300ms for small text generation endpoint; average token cost < $0.002 (pilot-level).

Outreach sequence (short multistep):
- Email 1 (intro + value): short subject, 2 sentence hook + single metric ask (15–20 min intro).
- Email 2 (use-case playbook): example of recommended rollout (post-purchase pilot), include a tiny mock (screenshot).
- Call: 30 min discovery + demo (bring sample receipts).
- Follow-up: technical deep-dive with infra/CTO; discuss Dedicated vs Hosted pricing and data controls.

Draft email (cold -> warm intro):
Subject: Quick idea for boosting post‑purchase revenue at Pebble
Hi Morgan — Samira from Redwood (we demoed at NRF). Short idea: run a 6‑week pilot that inserts lightweight, personalized suggestions into receipts — customers we’ve worked with saw ~2x CTR on offers and measurable AOV lift. Can I grab 20 mins next week to show one mock and the quick infra plan?

Call script (first discovery):
- 0–5: quick intros, remind NRF context.
- 5–12: problem framing — how are receipts & post-purchase offers working today? metrics?
- 12–20: run through 2 hypothesis + pilot design (what we’ll measure).
- 20–28: high level infra + security Qs (data residency, retention, PIIs).
- 28–30: next steps — run pilot? technical deep dive?

Objection handling (common ones + suggested responses):
- Objection: "We use vendor X for embeddings already — not worth moving."
  Response: "Totally — we can run a compatibility pilot: keep your vector DB, route inference to Redwood for generation/rerank. Compare per-API token/unit economics and latencies in week 1. No migration needed for pilot."
- Objection: "We worry about cost spikes with generative responses."
  Response: "Pilot uses constrained output templates + prefix caching and per-request length caps. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization + batching to hit cost targets you set; we can set hard budget guardrails in the pilot contract."
- Objection: "Security/PII — we prefer on-prem."
  Response: "We offer Private deployments and can do a VPC setup or dedicated capacity. For pilots we also offer encryption-in-transit and customer-managed KMS; contractually constrain logs/retention per your policy."

Technical pilot skeleton (minimal viable pilot):
- Scope: 2 stores (regionally representative), ~10k weekly receipts ingested, A/B split for post-purchase message.
- Integration points: webhook from backend -> Redwood endpoint for templated generation; store generated text in Postgres, render in receipt UI.
- Safety: templated outputs with blacklist, simple regex PII strip, logging only IDs (no raw receipt text retained after 14 days).
- Ops: weekly sync, Slack channel + shared dashboard (Console) for latency/cost.

Pricing/ask language (to test):
- Pilot proposal: 6 weeks, flat pilot fee $8k + usage up to $1.5k (capped). Optional follow-on: Dedicated reserve (quarterly commit).

Open questions / research items (TODO):
- Get baseline CTR / receipt volume from Pebble (ask in discovery).
- Confirm whether they already have an enrichment pipeline for receipts (Segment).
- Who signs pilot SOW? Presume Head of Ops + legal — need contacts.
- Check if they have specific latency SLOs for in-store POS assistant (would change architecture).

Action items (short):
- [Samira] Send first outreach email to Morgan + Lina (by EOD Wed).
- [Jamal] Draft slim pilot SOW (2 pager) and slot pricing options (due Fri).
- [Priya] Prepare 1–2 mock receipts showing recommended copy variants (by Tue).
- Schedule quick 30 min internal sync (gto-market + solutions eng) to align on ask/tech cameo.

Notes to self:
- Keep messaging low-friction — they are price sensitive. Lead with measurable uplift and low engineering lift.
- Offer comparison matrix: Redwood hosted vs their current provider (cost/latency/controls) — small table for sales deck.
- Consider offering a 30‑day cheap pilot as an alternative to $8k if they push back.

Random helpful links/refs:
- Example mock screenshots stored in: /shared_drives/company/mkt/samples/pebble-mocks (ask Mkt).
- Internal: Redwood Optimize playbook (Confluence) for batching/quantization notes.

End of scratch — messy. Will refine into a 1‑pager and short outbound sequence after internal sync.
